identity: An Arabic Islamic-knowledge multiple-choice quiz bank (trivia worksheet), 20 items long. Each item occupies one <NL>-delimited line and consists of a short interrogative stem followed by its 3-4 answer options run together with no punctuation, no option letters and no separators. Topics: sira (the mother of the Prophet), epithets of Companions (sayf Allah al-maslul, tarjuman al-Quran, dhu al-nurayn), Quranic suras and their names, the tajwid ruling on mim sakina, battles (Muta, Ayn Jalut), and the fiqh of hajj and jumua. Two items (15 and 18) are yes/no and carry only two options. The text has typing artifacts (sawa for surat at index 79, azwa for ghazwat at index 101), normal for a scraped quiz sheet. This is doctrine register S (MCQ/quiz) with J (worksheet) layout - it is not running prose of any kind.
law: The unit is a LAYOUT SLOT, not a syntactic sentence: [stem] || [option] || [option] || ... per line. Consequences. (1) The stem is ONE segment however long, absorbing every embedded proper name, Quranic quotation, isolated letter-example and honorific eulogy (S1). (2) Each option is ONE segment however short, including bare one-word options and numeral+noun pairs (S2). (3) Never cut inside a name (X bn Y), a hijri date (N ha), a numeral plus its counted noun (8 abwab), a place phrase (fi X), or the eulogy salla llahu alayhi wa-sallam (A1, A2). (4) Every token immediately before an <NL>, and the final token, closes a segment; an <NL> never carries one. (5) The stem/option seam is found by the first repeated option-initial cue (surat, marakat, ghazwat, fi, ayyam, abwab, bn) or, where no cue exists, at the point where the interrogative frame is syntactically complete and the candidate answers begin. Critically, LAW 3 (comma-lists, bare-NP runs and appositions WELD) does NOT reach into this register: its weld cases were all lists functioning as a constituent INSIDE a running sentence, whereas here the run IS the option layout. Same-register gold splits bare one-word options (|| sah || khata ||, || ghayr-sahih || sahih ||) and bare NP options (... huwa || al-ulum al-insaniyya wa-l-ijtimaiyya || al-ulum al-tatbiqiyya ||). Doctrine checklist item 4 ranks every MCQ option as a FREE boundary, in the same tier as <NL>.
reasoning: Register first (checklist step 1). All twenty <NL> lines open with an interrogative (man hiya, man huwa, ma, ma hiya, fi ayy, kam, hal, ayna, bi-madha, mata) or with the completion frame yutabar, and each closes with a run of mutually exclusive same-shaped candidates. That is an MCQ bank, so the unit system is stem/option and the printed-full-stop default of LAW 0-prime never applies here. I then walked every line looking for the stem/option seam. HARD SITE 1, item 3 index 42 (nun). The isolated letter nun is the CONTENT of the stem - the question asks which sura opens with the disconnected letter nun - so it welds into the stem and the first option starts at 43 with surat al-Qalam. Cutting before or after nun would be exactly the stem-internal cut that was my whole residual error in doc_1c49614cd6bc. Confidence hi. HARD SITE 2, item 7 index 115 (bi-hadiyya). The stem embeds a Quranic quotation under qawluhu taala. S1 is explicit that a Quranic quotation inside a stem welds (its at-316 and at-443 cases), and G1 that a speech verb never separates from its quote. So the stem runs its full nine tokens to bi-hadiyya and the four tajwid terms after it are the options. My batch-1 reflex would have cut at taala; that reflex is dead. Confidence hi. HARD SITE 3, items 12, 13 and 19 - runs of bare single-token options (al-Siddiq / al-Hakim / al-Amin / al-Karim; al-Haila / al-Madaji / al-Kalim / al-Tawdi; al-Iman / al-Islam / al-Salat / al-Siyam). These are formally the very bare-NP runs LAW 3 tells me to weld, and LAW 3 is the loudest lesson in my file (the thirteen-name Latin-gloss run, the five Cairo bridges, the bride adjectives). I split them anyway. The reason is that every LAW 3 weld case was a list serving as a constituent inside a running sentence, whereas an answer option is not a constituent of the stem at all - it is a separate layout slot. The direct same-register evidence is the true/false worksheets, where single-token options split, and the MCQ gold, where bare NP options split. Deferring to LAW 3 here would be a global prior overriding a local unit system, which is precisely the failure LAW 9 names. Confidence hi. HARD SITE 4, item 14 indices 222, 224, 226 (ha). The options are hijri years: 1 ha, 2 ha, 3 ha, 4 ha. A2 forbids cutting inside a number, and ha is the era marker bound to its digit just as an honorific binds to its name (A1), so each boundary falls after ha and never after a bare digit. I mark these med rather than hi because A2 was established on decimals (the 0.2 percent case) and I am extrapolating it to an era abbreviation inside an option list. HARD SITE 5, item 19 - the only seam in the document with no repeated lexical cue. Parse (a): the stem is yutabar al-hajj min arkan, ending at 276 on a dangling construct-state head that is still awaiting its complement, followed by four options. Parse (b): the stem is ...min arkan al-Iman, ending at 277, followed by three options. Parse (a) wins on two grounds. First, (b) makes the item incoherent as a quiz - hajj is a pillar of Islam and not of iman, so under (b) nothing is actually being asked and the remaining options answer nothing. Second, 276 has exactly the shape of the S1 gold whose stem ends on a dangling copula (...ulum al-lugha al-arabiyya huwa ||). Four options also matches the dominant pattern of this document; the only two-option items are the explicit yes/no ones, 15 and 18. The useful consequence of running both parses is that 277 is a boundary under EITHER reading - first-option end under (a), stem end under (b) - so all the risk is concentrated on 276 alone. Hence med at 276 and hi at 277 through 280. ROUTINE SITES, all resolved by never cutting inside a name. The X bn Y triples (Amr bn al-As, Khalid bn al-Walid, Uthman bn Affan, Khuzayma bn Thabit) are single options, as are the two four-token names Sad bn Abi Waqqas (62-65) and Jafar bn Abi Talib (189-192); option length varies freely within a line and that is not evidence of a boundary. In item 1 the eulogy salla llahu alayhi wa-sallam welds to al-Rasul, so the stem ends at 7 (A1). In item 6 the stem carries the name Jafar bn Abi Talib as its subject and ends at 96, after which the ghazwat-initial run is the options; the stem own ghazwat at 90 is governed by fi ayy and is not an option. In items 17 and 20 each numeral is paired with its counted noun (arbaat ayyam, 8 abwab) per A2, so the boundaries land on ayyam and abwab and never on a digit. The typos sawa at 79 and azwa at 101 are artifacts that weld option-initially (A2b); they are not boundaries and they do not disturb the surat-X and ghazwat-X option shapes. FREE BOUNDARIES. All twenty tokens immediately preceding an <NL>, plus the final token 293, are boundaries, and each of them is also the last option of its item, so the layout law and the format rule agree everywhere - a good consistency check on the whole reading. ERROR POSTURE. My known bias in this register is cutting inside stems, so at every seam I asked whether the material was still part of what is being ASKED; wherever it was, I welded.
